column1: # Registry of every ADR Confirmation. Tab-separated.
# This file is the reason an architecture decision cannot quietly stop being enforced.
# Every ADR in docs/adr/ carries a Confirmation naming a runnable command. Each one is
# registered here exactly once, in one of two states:
#   ACTIVE   the check runs today, in dod.sh or security-invariants.sh
#   PENDING  the check cannot run yet, with a REASON and a TRIGGER that closes it
# There is no third state. A Confirmation that is neither ACTIVE nor PENDING is a
# boundary nobody is holding, and dod.sh fails when it finds one, because a check that
# should apply but cannot run is a failure and not a skip.
# PENDING is never silent. dod.sh prints every pending row on every run, so the list
# is uncomfortable to look at and gets shorter.
